questions.q: How did Stoicism begin, according to the summary?
a: Zeno lost everything in a shipwreck and turned to philosophy
Marcus Aurelius wrote down his private meditations
Cicero studied philosophy in Athens as a young man
Crates opened a school for wealthy Roman senators
questions.why: The first lesson says Zeno survived a devastating shipwreck that cost him his livelihood, then moved to Athens to study philosophy.

questions.q: What are the four guiding virtues of Stoicism?
a: Courage, wisdom, temperance and justice
Honesty, loyalty, patience and humility
Discipline, ambition, generosity and faith
Courage, strength, honor and duty
questions.why: The summary names courage, wisdom, temperance and justice as the principles Zeno's philosophy was built on.

questions.q: Where does the name Stoicism come from?
a: The porch in Athens where Zeno taught
The Greek word for enduring hardship
The name of Zeno's first teacher
A Roman general who spread the ideas
questions.why: Zeno taught on a porch called the Stoa Poikile, and the philosophy took its name from that simple porch.

questions.q: How did Cicero fall short of Stoic ideals?
a: He had Catiline's supporters executed without a trial
He refused to serve as consul of Rome
He gave away his family fortune to the poor
He abandoned philosophy for a military career
questions.why: The second lesson says anger got the better of Cicero, and he killed thousands without trial, staining his legacy.

questions.q: How did Marcus Aurelius show humility as emperor?
a: He shared power with his brother and forgave conspirators
He refused to read any philosophy while ruling
He raised taxes to refill the Roman treasury
He sent his old tutors away from the palace
questions.why: The third lesson says his first act was to make his adoptive brother co-emperor, and he forgave Cassius's conspirators.
